chunks: And that the pillars upon which Islam is built are five: prayer, alms, fasting, Hajj, and the walaya of the Prophet and the Imams (blessings of Allah be upon them) after him. And they are twelve Imams. The first of them is the Commander of the Believers Ali son of Abi Talib, then al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, then Ali son of al-Husayn, then al-Baqir Muhammad son of Ali, then as-Sadiq Ja'far son of Muhammad, then al-Kadhim Musa son of Ja'far, then al-Rida Ali son of Musa, then al-Jawad Muhammad son of Ali, then al-Hadi Ali son of Muhammad, then al-'Askari al-Hasan son of Ali, then al-Hujjat son of al-Hasan son of Ali (peace be upon them),

and the acknowledgment that they are the possessors of the command whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded to be obeyed, and He said: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and the possessors of the command from among you.' And that their obedience is obedience to Allah, and disobedience to them is disobedience to Allah. Their friend is the friend of Allah, and their enemy is the enemy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

And the love of the progeny of the Prophet (may the blessings of Allah be upon him and his family), when they are upon the course of their purified fathers, is an obligatory duty incumbent on the necks of the servants until the Day of the Resurrection, and it is the wage of the prophethood, due to the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Say: I do not ask you for it any wage except the love for the near kin.'

key_terms.أولوا الأمر: possessors of the command: Quranic title for those whose obedience is divinely mandated (4:59)
key_terms.الدعائم: the pillars: the foundational obligations of Islam
key_terms.فريضة واجبة: obligatory duty: a binding religious obligation on all believers
key_terms.مودة: love/affection: obligatory love for the Prophet's kin as the wage of prophethood (42:23)
key_terms.ولاية: walaya/authority: spiritual and political authority of the Prophet and Imams

ai.seo_question: What are the five pillars of Islam according to Shia belief, and who are the twelve Imams?
ai.summary: This passage enumerates the five pillars of Islam -- prayer, alms, fasting, Hajj, and the walaya of the Prophet and the twelve Imams -- listing all twelve Imams by name from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali b. Abi Talib to al-Hujjat b. al-Hasan. It then establishes that obeying these Imams is obeying Allah, and disobeying them is disobeying Allah. Love for the Prophet's purified progeny is declared an obligatory duty until the Day of Resurrection, identified as the 'wage of prophethood' cited in Quran 42:23.

en.bilal-muhammad: The pillars upon which Islam is built are five: prayer, alms, fasting, Hajj, and the walaya of the Prophet and the Imams (s) after him. There are twelve Imams. The first of them is Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib, then al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, then `Ali b. al-Husayn, then al-Baqir Muhammad b. `Ali, then as-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad, then al-Kadhim Musa b. Ja`far, then al-Rida `Ali b. Musa, then al-Jawad Muhammad b. `Ali, then al-Hadi `Ali b. Muhammad, then al-`Askari al-Hasan b. `Ali, then al-Hujjat b. al-Hasan b. `Ali (as).

[The Imami religion is] confirmation that they are the Masters of the Order (ulil amr) whose obedience Allah commanded. So, He said “Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and the possessors of the command from you” [4:59] The obedience to them is obedience to Allah, and disobedience to them is disobedience to Allah. Their friend (wali) is the friend of Allah, and their enemy is the enemy of Allah.

Love for the progeny of the Prophet (s), when they are upon the course of their purified fathers, is a obligatory duty on the necks of the servants until the Day of the Resurrection, and it is the wage of the prophethood, due to the saying of Allah, “Say: I do not ask a wage of you but love of the near kin” [42:23].
